1. The event has always been open to all family members.
2. The person hosting didn't intentionally exclude anyone; they relied on established tradition.
3. The upset family member could have reached out to confirm or simply attended as in previous years.
4. The responsibility for feeling included might also lie with the attendees to recognize the open invitation.

Thus, the action is morally acceptable.
